# Cornelia Bryant

## Overview

- **Age:** 59 years old  <sub>[v5 c26 P26](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0026)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Status:** married  <sub>[v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss Cornelia  <sub>[v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)</sub>; Mrs. Marshall Elliott  <sub>[v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

She has a fresh, round, pink-and-white face with jolly, kindly brown eyes. Her fair hair is styled in a tight little knob on her head, held by an elastic band, as she refuses to use hat pins. She possesses a comfortable, matronly figure and does not look like a traditional old maid.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c11 P17](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0017), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)_

## Personality

Known as a notorious man-hater, she constantly criticizes men and holds a strong prejudice against Methodists. Despite her bitter tongue and outspoken, opinionated nature, she possesses an exceptionally kind heart and is always willing to help those in trouble. She is pragmatic, generous, deeply caring toward children, and considers herself a lonely soul who values true friends.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P38](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0038), [v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c8 P27](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0027), [v4 c8 P76](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0076), [v4 c19 P41](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0041)_

## History

Cornelia Bryant grew up in Four Winds as the daughter of Stephen Bryant. After her mother's death, she acted as mother and sister to her younger brother, whose early death in his twenties deeply grieved her. Despite receiving suitors in her youth, she remained unmarried for many years, earning a reputation as a sharp-tongued old maid with an underlying generosity toward anyone in trouble. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe moved to Four Winds, she quickly formed a close friendship with Anne and regularly visited them, frequently engaging in lighthearted debates with Captain Jim. She took a protective interest in Leslie Moore and helped look out for her well-being. Eventually, she accepted the marriage proposal of her long-time acquaintance Marshall Elliott and had been married to him for thirteen years by the time the Meredith family settled at the Glen St. Mary manse. Learning of the mistreatment of the orphan Mary Vance, Cornelia had her husband investigate and took the girl into her home to raise her, growing fond of her as a helpful companion.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P40](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0040), [v4 c8 P19](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0019), [v4 c8 P75](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0075), [v4 c10 P38](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0038), [v4 c15 P7](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0007), [v4 c15 P41](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0041), [v4 c34 P28](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0028), [v4 c37 P8](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0008), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c8 P4](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0004), [v5 c9 P38](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0038), [v5 c26 P26](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0026)_

## Background by volume

- was an only child for eight years before her younger brother was born  <sub>[v4 c34 P26](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0026)</sub>
- named after her mother, Anne  <sub>[v4 c8 P79](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0079), [v4 c34 P26](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0026)</sub>
- raised her younger brother after their mother died when he was under three  <sub>[v4 c34 P28](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0028)</sub>
- her only brother died when he was in his twenties  <sub>[v4 c28 P7](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0007), [v4 c34 P28](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0028)</sub>
- had a suitor named Amos Grant in her youth  <sub>[v4 c37 P16](../source/v04-c37.md#nw-v04-c37-p0016)</sub>
- won first prize for lemon pies at the Charlottetown Exhibition ten years prior  <sub>[v4 c10 P35](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0035)</sub>
